title: Curve pullback is faithful on the canonically polarized Jacobian
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $C/k$ be a smooth projective connected curve of genus $g\geq2$ [def-sc-curves], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-genus], and fix its degree-zero Picard variety $J=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$, with its representing isomorphism [sk-thm-picard-main], [def-sc-jacobian]. Then $J$ has a canonical principal polarization $\lambda_C$, induced by the theta divisor (the image of effective divisors [def-sc-divisor] of degree $g-1$ after translating $\operatorname{Pic}^{g-1}_{C/k}$ to $J$); the induced polarization does not depend on the translation. A polarization of an abelian variety $A$ over an algebraically closed field means a homomorphism $\lambda:A\to A^\vee$ induced by an ample [def-sc-ample] invertible sheaf [def-sc-invertible-module] $L$, namely $x\mapsto[t_x^*L\otimes L^{-1}]$, where $t_x$ is translation by $x$ and $A^\vee=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{A/k}$ is the dual abelian variety representing algebraically trivial invertible sheaves, rigidified at the identity. A polarization is principal when $\lambda$ is an isomorphism. For a group automorphism $a$ of $A$ (an automorphism of the $k$-group scheme $A$ [def-sc-group-scheme]), its dual $a^\vee$ is pullback on $A^\vee$; preserving $\lambda$ means $a^\vee\lambda a=\lambda$. Every $k$-automorphism $u$ of $C$ induces a $k$-group automorphism $a_u$ of $J$, whose action on the Picard functor is pullback of invertible sheaves along $u\times\mathrm{id}_T:C\times_kT\to C\times_kT$ for every $k$-scheme $T$. It preserves $\lambda_C$, and the assignment $u\mapsto a_u$ is injective as a map of sets. In particular $a_u=\mathrm{id}_J$ implies $u=\mathrm{id}_C$.

source.place: Chapter III §6 (canonical theta polarization, especially Theorem 6.6 and discussion 6.11), printed pp.105–108, and Theorem 12.1(b), printed p.120 (uniqueness for a fixed sign, including hyperelliptic curves). Pullback gives the inverse of the usual covariant Jacobian automorphism.

proof.text: Choose $P\in C(k)$ by [lem-pc-rational-points-dense]. Apply [lem-sfb-symmetric-abel-image-geometry] to the given representing Jacobian: write $f=f_P$, let $\mathcal M_P$ be its normalized universal family, and set $\Theta=W_{g-1}$. This constructs the theta divisor as the scheme-theoretic image of effective divisors, after tensoring with $\mathcal O_C(-(g-1)P)$. In particular it is an effective Cartier divisor, so $\mathcal O_J(\Theta)$ is an actual invertible sheaf, not a choice from a mere existence assertion.

source.place: III §§1–2, Theorem 5.1(a), and the paragraph before Theorem 6.6, pp.88–105

proof.text:
Use [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] to form $J^\vee$ and its normalized Poincare sheaf $\mathcal P_J$. Pull this sheaf back along $f\times1$. By [sk-thm-picard-main] it gives a map $J^\vee\to\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$. Since $J^\vee$ is connected and its identity maps to the trivial sheaf, the open degree decomposition in that node forces this map into $\operatorname{Pic}^0_{C/k}$. Its normalized representing map $\delta:J^\vee\to J$ exists by [lem-sfb-symmetric-abel-image-geometry]; it is a homomorphism because tensoring families represents addition. Put $\lambda=\phi_{\mathcal O_J(\Theta)}$. For $L=\mathcal O_J(\Theta^-)$, the polarization calculus gives $\phi_L=\lambda$, and $L_0\cong(1\times\lambda)^*\mathcal P_J$. The sheaf identity [lem-sfb-theta-poincare-pullback] therefore reads
$$(1\times(\delta\lambda[-1]))^*\mathcal M_P\cong\mathcal M_P.$$
The representing universal property of $\mathcal M_P$ gives $\delta\lambda[-1]=\mathrm{id}_J$ as scheme morphisms. Since these are homomorphisms, $(-\delta)\lambda=\mathrm{id}_J$. This is an identity of families, so it detects infinitesimal kernels as well as geometric points.

source.place: III Lemmas 6.8(b) and 6.9, pp.106–107; I §8 universal family

proof.text: The dual dimension formula in [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] gives $\dim J^\vee=\dim J=g$. Apply [lem-sfb-equal-dimension-abelian-retract] to $s=\lambda$ and $r=-\delta$: $\lambda$ is an isomorphism. Since $\Theta$ is effective, the effective-divisor ampleness criterion of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] now shows that $\mathcal O_J(\Theta)$ is ample. Thus $\lambda$ is a principal polarization, with precisely the convention $x\mapsto[t_x^*L\otimes L^{-1}]$ in the statement.

source.place: III Theorem 6.6 and Lemma 6.9, pp.105–107; I Proposition 8.1 and Remark 8.2

proof.text: An identification of $\operatorname{Pic}^{g-1}_{C/k}$ with $J$ by tensoring with the inverse of a degree-$(g-1)$ line bundle differs from the chosen one by a translation: the quotient of two such line bundles has degree zero and hence is a point of $J$. Therefore the effective image divisor is replaced by a translate of $\Theta$. The equality $\phi_{t_b^*L}=\phi_L$ from [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] proves that the induced polarization is independent of this identification (and in particular of $P$). Define $\lambda_C=\lambda$.

source.place: III paragraph before Theorem 6.6, p.105, and Summary 6.11, p.108

proof.text: For every $k$-scheme $T$, pullback along $u\times\mathrm{id}_T$ sends a fibrewise degree-zero line bundle on $C\times T$ to one of the same degree, commutes with tensor product and with all base changes in $T$, and preserves bundles pulled back from $T$. It thus gives a natural group automorphism of the fppf Picard functor and of its degree-zero part; the inverse is pullback along $u^{-1}\times\mathrm{id}_T$. Through the given representing isomorphism [def-sc-jacobian], Yoneda [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] produces the group-scheme automorphism $a_u$ and its inverse. This construction has the required effect on every $T$, including nonreduced $T$. Pullback reverses composition, so $a_{uv}=a_va_u$.

source.place: III §1, Theorems 1.6–1.7, pp.88–89; pullback on represented functors

proof.text:
Let $L_0=\mathcal O_C((g-1)P)$ and $c=[u^*L_0\otimes L_0^{-1}]\in J(k)$. In the coordinates $\operatorname{Pic}^{g-1}\to J$, $N\mapsto[N\otimes L_0^{-1}]$, the pullback $u^*$ is $x\mapsto a_u(x)+c$. Pullback by an isomorphism permutes effective divisors; hence it preserves their scheme-theoretic image. Using the construction of [lem-sfb-symmetric-abel-image-geometry], this gives $t_c a_u(\Theta)=\Theta$ as divisors. Consequently $a_u^{-1}(\Theta)=t_{a_u^{-1}(c)}(\Theta)$, a translate. The flat-pullback identity [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-flat-pullback] (an isomorphism is flat) identifies $a_u^*\mathcal O_J(\Theta)$ with the bundle of this divisor. Translation invariance and the pullback formula of [lem-sfb-abelian-polarization-calculus] now give
$$a_u^\vee\lambda_Ca_u=\phi_{a_u^*\mathcal O_J(\Theta)}=\phi_{\mathcal O_J(\Theta)}=\lambda_C.$$

source.place: III §5, effective image description, p.100; I §§8–9, line-bundle homomorphisms and dual pullback

proof.text:
Assume $a_u=\mathrm{id}_J$ and write $w=u^{-1}$. The action just constructed and [lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-flat-pullback], applied to the point divisors on $C$, give
$$[\mathcal O_C(w(Q)-w(R))]=u^*[\mathcal O_C(Q-R)]=[\mathcal O_C(Q-R)]$$
for all $Q,R\in C(k)$. By the divisor-class isomorphism [lem-sc-divisor-class-curve],
$$w(Q)+R\sim Q+w(R).$$
Here $\sim$ denotes linear equivalence of divisors; this step uses the inverse $w$, rather than identifying pullback with the covariant Jacobian action.

source.place: III §2, divisor-class description on pp.91–92, and the proof of Theorem 12.1(b), p.120

proof.text: Suppose $w\ne\mathrm{id}_C$. There is a point $R\in C(k)$ with $w(R)\ne R$: otherwise the two morphisms agree on the dense rational points from [lem-pc-rational-points-dense], and hence on $C$. Indeed their equalizer is closed since $C$ is separated, and its ideal is zero: on any affine open a section vanishing at a dense set of points vanishes, since $C$ is integral and thus reduced by [lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings]. This is also a direct justification of scheme equality, not just equality of underlying sets. Choose distinct $Q_1,Q_2\in C(k)\setminus\{R\}$. Such points exist by applying the same density theorem twice to the complements of the finitely many points already chosen: these are nonempty smooth opens because $C$ is integral of dimension one.

source.place: III proof of Theorem 12.1(b), p.120, choosing distinct points; elementary reduced-scheme equalizer argument

proof.text: For $i=1,2$ put $D_i=w(Q_i)+R$ and $E_i=Q_i+w(R)$. They are effective divisors of degree two, and step 7 gives $D_i\sim E_i$. They are distinct: if they were equal, the occurrence of $R$ on the right would force $R=Q_i$ or $R=w(R)$, both excluded. Thus $|D_i|$ has two distinct members. Apply [lem-sfb-degree-two-pencil-uniqueness] using $g\geq2$. Both systems $|D_1|$ and $|D_2|$ must be the same basepoint-free degree-two pencil, and exactly one of its members contains $R$. Since both $D_i$ contain $R$, $D_1=D_2$. Cancel $R$ in the free abelian divisor group [def-sc-divisor] to obtain $w(Q_1)=w(Q_2)$, contrary to injectivity of $w$. Hence $w=\mathrm{id}_C$ and $u=\mathrm{id}_C$. This argument covers hyperelliptic curves and characteristic two.

source.place: III proof of Theorem 12.1(b), p.120, fixed-sign uniqueness argument with its varying-points contradiction made explicit

proof.text: Finally, if $a_u=a_v$, contravariance from step 5 gives $a_{u v^{-1}}=a_{v^{-1}}a_u=a_v^{-1}a_v=\mathrm{id}_J$. Steps 7–9 imply $u v^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_C$, hence $u=v$. This proves the asserted injectivity as a map of sets.

source.place: III Theorem 12.1(b), fixed-sign uniqueness, p.120; elementary composition

proof_origin.place: III §§1–2, 5–6 (construction, Lemmas 6.8–6.9), and proof of Theorem 12.1(b), p.120; functoriality written using the representing Picard functor.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q59-d889d42c2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: I read the item's ten steps and all five new statement-only nodes in full, checked them against Milne's Abelian Varieties, and made no changes. Context: this is the first split (the base had no proof), the item is not dropped, it is still unsplit on live, and its citer geometric-curve-level-faithfulness uses exactly the stated clauses. Source matches: theta-poincare-pullback is exactly Milne III 6.8(b) on printed p.106, with Θ^- = [-1]^*Θ (the text extraction loses the minus sign). Step 2 then gives δλ[-1]=id, so (−δ)λ=id, agreeing with f^∨ = −φ^{-1} in III 6.11. I checked the rigidification along P×J^∨ (f(P)=0) and the degree-0 argument (connected J^∨ plus the open degree decomposition in sk-thm-picard-main). The equal-dimension retract statement is true (s is a closed immersion; equal dimension on the reduced irreducible B makes it surjective, hence an iso). It upgrades the one-sided inverse to principal. Step 3 uses the converse of I 8.1, effective D with finite K(L) ⇒ ample. Milne states it ('D ample iff φ_{L(D)} isogeny', III 6.5 and I 8.2) but leaves that direction unproved; it is true by Mumford §6 App. 1. This is noted for whoever splits the calculus node later. Step 6: I rechecked t_c a_u(Θ)=Θ ⇒ a_u^{-1}Θ = Θ + a_u^{-1}(c), which gives a_u^∨λa_u=λ by translation invariance. Steps 7–9 are Milne III 12.1(b) written out: pullback of point divisors uses w=u^{-1}; D_i ≠ E_i because R≠Q_i and R≠w(R); the unique basepoint-free g^1_2 with one member through R gives D_1=D_2 and a contradiction. This covers hyperelliptic curves and characteristic 2. The pencil node is true and needs g≥2, as Hartshorne IV 5.3 (recalled by Milne). Abel-image node: birationality for r≤g is III 5.1(a), M_P is III 1.7, and the closed immersion is III 2.3. W_{g-1} is Cartier because J is smooth. Edge cases g=1 and r=0 hold. No duplicates: rg -L for dual/Poincaré/theta/hyperelliptic/g^1_2/isogeny/polarization matched only these nodes, the item, its citer and odd-level-rigidity. No new node restates a clause of the item. Batch-5 findings: the def-sc-jacobian citations (×2) and the thm-pc-hilb-curves citation add 0 nodes to the item's base statement closure, since both are reached via the existing stmt_deps sk-thm-picard-main/def-sc-jacobian. The flagged endpoints, def-pod-ring-scalar-extension (a general scalar-extension definition) and lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near (a general scheme fact), are not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so I accepted them.
